title: How to Play Heteronym: Rules, Tips, and Strategies for Beginners
description: New to Heteronym? Learn the rules, scoring, hints system, and expert strategies to solve daily heteronym puzzles faster and build your streak.

content.text: Heteronym is a daily word puzzle that challenges your lateral thinking and vocabulary. Each puzzle gives you two clues — and you must find the single word that connects them both. The twist? The answer is always a heteronym: a word spelled the same but with different meanings (and often different pronunciations).

For example, the clues 'to guide' and 'a heavy metal' both point to 'lead'. The clues 'to rip' and 'a drop from your eye' both point to 'tear'. You're not guessing letters — you're making a semantic leap between two seemingly unrelated concepts.
The game is simple to understand but tricky to master:

items.definition: You're shown two clues. Each describes a different meaning of the same hidden word. Think about what concept connects them.
Enter a word you think matches both clues. Submit it and the game will tell you if you're correct.
If you're stuck, you can reveal a hint. The first hint is free — subsequent hints cost one life each.
Each wrong guess costs one life. You start with 4 lives. Lose all 4 and the puzzle is over.
If you solve the daily puzzle, you can share your result (in violet emoji grid format, just like Wordle) with friends.

content.text: Heteronym offers two ways to play:

items.definition: One new puzzle every day, the same for everyone worldwide. Your streak, win rate, and stats are tracked. Share your result and challenge friends to beat your score.
Practice mode with random puzzles from the archive. No streak pressure — just build your skills and vocabulary. A running score tracks your total points across sessions.

content.text: Understanding the scoring system helps you make strategic decisions:

items.definition: Every wrong guess costs 1 life. Use hints strategically — the first is free, but each subsequent hint also costs 1 life.
Solve without hints: 3 points. With 1 hint used: 2 points. With 2+ hints: 1 point. Points accumulate in Free Play mode.
Solve the daily puzzle on consecutive days to build your streak. Miss a day and it resets. Your longest streak is tracked separately.
If you're completely stuck, you can reveal the answer — but it counts as a loss and breaks your streak.

content.text: Here are some proven strategies to improve your solve rate:

items.definition: If Clue 1 is a verb and Clue 2 is a noun, you're looking for a word that works as both. Many heteronyms are noun-verb pairs (record, produce, contract, object).

Common heteronym pattern: the noun is stressed on the first syllable (RE-cord, OB-ject), the verb on the second (re-CORD, ob-JECT). If the two clues feel like different parts of speech, this pattern is your friend.
The first hint is free, but don't burn it immediately. Spend a few minutes thinking first — then use it to confirm or redirect your thinking.
If you think of a word that might work but aren't sure, look it up. Heteronyms have distinct dictionary entries with different pronunciations.
Like any puzzle, you get better with practice. The daily format trains your brain to think in heteronym patterns over time.

content.text: A heteronym is a word that:

items.definition: Both meanings use the exact same letters — no changes, no accents.
The two meanings are unrelated or distantly related (lead as 'to guide' vs lead as 'the metal').
Unlike homonyms (which sound the same), heteronyms sound different. Wind (air) rhymes with 'grinned'; wind (to twist) rhymes with 'find'.

content.text: Heteronyms are different from homophones (sound the same, spelled differently — like 'there/their/they're') and homographs (spelled the same, could sound the same or different — heteronyms are a subset of homographs that sound different).

After completing the daily puzzle, you can generate a challenge link. Share it with friends and see who can solve it faster. Each challenge link shares the same puzzle so you're comparing on equal footing.
Your friend clicks the link, plays the puzzle, and their result is independent from yours — but you can compare scores to see who solved in fewer guesses.

Whether you're a word game veteran or brand new to heteronyms, the daily puzzle takes just a few minutes and exercises a different part of your brain than Wordle or Connections. One puzzle a day keeps your vocabulary sharp.
